'''Daniel Amihud Lidar'''<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://viterbi.usc.edu/directory/faculty/Lidar/Daniel | title=USC - Viterbi School of Engineering - Viterbi Faculty Directory}}</ref>; born 1968) is the holder of the Viterbi Professorship of Engineering at the [[University of Southern California]], where he is a professor of electrical engineering, chemistry, physics & astronomy. He is the director and co-founder of the [[University of Southern California|USC]] [[Center for Quantum Information Science & Technology]] (CQIST), the director of the USC-IBM Quantum Innovation Center,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://viterbischool.usc.edu/mediacoverage/usc-opens-first-ibm-quantum-innovation-center-on-the-west-coast/|title=USC-IBM Quantum Innovation Center}}</ref> as well as scientific director of the [[USC-Lockheed Martin Quantum Computing Center]], notable for his research on control of [[quantum system]]s and [[quantum information processing]].

==Education==
He is a class of 1986 graduate of the [[Armand Hammer United World College of the American West]]. He obtained his PhD from the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] in 1997 under Robert Benny Gerber <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholars.huji.ac.il/robertbennygerber/biocv/cv|title=Robert Benny Gerber}}</ref> and [[Ofer Biham]], with a thesis entitled ''Structural Characterization of Disordered Systems''.

==Career==
In 1997–2000, he was a postdoc at [[UC Berkeley]], having been awarded Rothschild Foundation<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.yadhanadiv.org.il/fellowship-prize/rothschild-fellowship |title = Rothschild Fellows &#124; Yad Hanadiv}}</ref> and [[Fulbright Program]] fellowships (the latter of which he declined){{citation needed|date=June 2018}}; in 2000–2005, he was an assistant professor and then later an associate professor of chemistry at the [[University of Toronto]], with cross-appointments in physics and mathematics. He moved to the [[University of Southern California]] in 2005, where he is a professor of [[electrical engineering]], [[chemistry]], and [[physics]].

==Honors==
He was a 2017 [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] recipient,<ref>[http://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/daniel-a-lidar/ Guggenheim Fellow]</ref> a 2007 Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]],<ref name="aps">{{cite news|title=2007 Fellows of the American Physical Society|url=http://www.aps.org/units/gqi/fellowship/index.cfm?year=2007|archive-date=September 29, 2012|access-date=March 3, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120929210018/http://www.aps.org/units/gqi/fellowship/index.cfm?year=2007}}</ref> a 2012 Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], and 2015 Fellow of the [[IEEE]]. He is listed as one of the top 20 authors of the decade 2000–2009 in [[Quantum Computing]] by [[Thomson Reuters]]' Sciencewatch.<ref>{{cite news|title=2010 ScienceWatch Quantum Computer interviews|url=http://archive.sciencewatch.com/ana/st/quantum/interview/}}</ref> In 2009 he was elected an Outstanding Referee <ref>{{cite news|title=List of Outstanding Referees of the APS|url=https://journals.aps.org/OutstandingReferees}}</ref> of the [[American Physical Society]]. His early career awards include a [[Sloan Foundation]] Fellowship, the Young Explorer Award given by the [[Canadian Institute for Advanced Research]] for the top 20 researchers in Canada under age 40, and the [[John Charles Polanyi]] Prize in Chemistry awarded by the Ontario Council of Graduate Studies.<ref name="jcp">{{cite news|title=List of John Charles Polanyi prize winners |url=http://ocgs.cou.on.ca/_bin/home/polanyi/prizeWinners.cfm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110706192502/http://ocgs.cou.on.ca/_bin/home/polanyi/prizeWinners.cfm |archive-date=July 6, 2011 }}</ref>

==Research==
He has made numerous contributions to [[quantum computing]] and [[quantum control]], and is the coeditor and coauthor of a book<ref>Daniel A. Lidar (editor) and Todd A. Brun (editor) (2013). "Quantum Error Correction". Cambridge University Press.</ref> on [[quantum error correction]]. His current work focuses on [[adiabatic quantum computing]] and [[quantum annealing]], areas where he has made widely cited contributions to studying the capabilities of the [[D-Wave Systems]] processors.<ref>{{cite journal|title= Defining and detecting quantum speedup |volume=345 |issue= 6195 |journal=Science |pages=420–424 |doi=10.1126/science.1252319 |pmid= 25061205 | last1 = Ronnow | first1 = T. F.|arxiv=1401.2910 |bibcode=2014Sci...345..420R |year= 2014 |s2cid=5596838 }}</ref> His past interests include [[scattering theory]] and [[fractals]]. Lidar's research in quantum information processing has focused primarily on methods for overcoming [[decoherence]]. He wrote some of the founding papers on [[decoherence-free subspaces]], most notably his widely cited paper "Decoherence-free subspaces for quantum computation",<ref>{{cite journal|title= Decoherence-Free Subspaces for Quantum Computation| doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.81.2594 |bibcode=1998PhRvL..81.2594L |volume=81 |issue= 12|journal=Physical Review Letters |pages=2594–2597|year= 1998|last1= Lidar|first1= D. A.|last2= Chuang|first2= I. L.|last3= Whaley|first3= K. B.|arxiv=quant-ph/9807004| s2cid=13979882 }}</ref> and their generalization, noiseless subsystems. These contributions were noted in his APS Fellow citation.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/units/gqi/fellowship/index.cfm?year= |title=APS Fellow citation |publisher=Aps.org |date=July 27, 2011 |access-date=January 4, 2012}}</ref> He has also made major contributions to [[dynamical decoupling]], in particular the invention of the concatenated dynamical decoupling (CDD) method.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=K. Khodjasteh and D.A. Lidar, "Fault-Tolerant Quantum Dynamical Decoupling", Phys. Rev. Lett. '''95''', 180501 (2005) |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=95 |issue=18 |article-number = 180501|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.95.180501 |pmid=16383882 |year=2005 |last1=Khodjasteh |first1=K. |last2=Lidar |first2=D. A. |bibcode=2005PhRvL..95r0501K|arxiv=quant-ph/0408128 |s2cid=9754216 }}</ref> He has made a proposal to protect [[adiabatic quantum computation]] against decoherence, using dynamical decoupling, one of the only proposals to date dealing with error correction for the adiabatic model.<ref>{{cite journal|url=http://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.100.160506 |title=Daniel A. Lidar, "Towards Fault Tolerant Adiabatic Quantum Computation", Phys. Rev. Lett. '''100''', 160506 (2008) |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.100.179904 |access-date=January 4, 2012 |bibcode=2008PhRvL.100q9904L |volume=100 |issue=17 |article-number=179904 |journal=Physical Review Letters | last1 = Lidar | first1 = Daniel A.|year=2008 |doi-access=free }}</ref> Lidar has also worked on quantum algorithms, having written some of the pioneering papers in the subject on simulation of classical statistical mechanics<ref>{{Cite journal|title=D.A. Lidar and O. Biham, "Simulating Ising Spin Glasses on a Quantum Computer", Phys. Rev. E '''56''', 3661 (1997) |journal=Physical Review E |volume=56 |issue=3 |page=3661 |publisher=Link.aps.org |date=February 12, 1997 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevE.56.3661 |last1=Lidar |first1=Daniel A. |last2=Biham |first2=Ofer |arxiv=quant-ph/9611038 |bibcode=1997PhRvE..56.3661L |s2cid=3686104 }}</ref> and quantum chemistry.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=D.A. Lidar and H. Wang, "Calculating the Thermal Rate Constant with Exponential Speedup on a Quantum Computer", Phys. Rev. E '''59''', 2429 (1999) |journal=Physical Review E |volume=59 |issue=2 |page=2429 |year=1999 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevE.59.2429 |last1=Lidar |first1=Daniel A. |last2=Wang |first2=Haobin |arxiv=quant-ph/9807009 |bibcode=1999PhRvE..59.2429L |s2cid=3735955 }}</ref> In his PhD work he made a widely cited observation on the limited scaling range of empirically observed [[fractals]],<ref>{{cite journal|author1=David Avnir |author2=Ofer Biham |author3=Daniel Lidar |author4=Ofer Malcai |title=  APPLIED MATHEMATICS:Is the Geometry of Nature Fractal?|date=January 2, 1998 |doi=10.1126/science.279.5347.39 |volume=279 |issue=5347 |journal=Science |pages=39–40|arxiv=cond-mat/9801038 |bibcode=1998Sci...279...39A |s2cid=3680350 }}</ref> which led to an exchange with [[Benoit Mandelbrot]].<ref>{{cite journal|url=http://www.sciencemag.org/cgi/content/full/279/5352/783c |title= Is Nature Fractal?|date=February 6, 1998 |access-date=January 4, 2012 |doi=10.1126/science.279.5352.783c |volume=279 |issue= 5352|journal=Science |pages=783c–783|last1= Mandelbrot|first1= B. B.|bibcode=1998Sci...279..783M|s2cid= 122791263|url-access=subscription}}</ref>
